title: What every involution gives, and what it does not — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
What every involution gives, and what it does not — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 8 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 28 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 8. Most binding: all (7), fixedPoints (3), constantSum (3), nine (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/involution.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 980210d1-24d9-8a7f-a759-3e28e4faa442. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 4, 5, 4, 1, 6, 3). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: priorart.lean (3 observed, 0.8 expected, lift 3.76), coin.lean (3 observed, 1.06 expected, lift 2.82), fnv.lean (3 observed, 1.06 expected, lift 2.82). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.39; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.47. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 37.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. that a permutation of order two decomposes a finite set into fixed points and transpositions, and that the number of fixed points therefore matches the parity of the set, is classical and long predates this deposit. It is the orbit-counting argument in any first course. What is this deposit's own here is the EXHAUSTIVE decision over ℤ/9 and the measured refusal below. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. there_are_2620_involutions_of_nine — all.length = 2620 record
  2. the_fuel_was_not_the_limit — (matchings 11 nine).length = all.length record
  3. every_involution_fixes_at_least_one_point — all.all (fun m => fixedPoints m ≥ 1) record
  4. the_fixed_points_are_always_odd — all.all (fun m => fixedPoints m % 2 == 1) record
  5. no_single_point_is_fixed_by_all — nine.all (fun d => ¬ all.all (fun m => m.contains (d, d))) record
  6. the_constant_sum_is_rare — (all.filter constantSum).length = 90 record
  7. so_involutions_are_not_all_harmonic_in_that_sense — ¬ all.all constantSum record
  8. the_coins_reflection_is_harmonic_and_is_one_of_the_ninety — constantSum coinLike = true ∧ fixedPoints coinLike = 1 ∧ (swaps coinLike).all (fun p => p.1 + p.2 == 9) record
